summary.locked_model: Sum of Voigt profiles (Lorentzian-dominant, Gaussian width free for shim/disorder) on a linear baseline: 1 Voigt for fast-exchange spectra (~-2.5 to -3.5 ppm), 2 Voigts for slow-exchange spectra (free TEP + Mg-coordinated TEP, ~-5.5 and ~-3.5 ppm).

detailed_analysis: The 31P NMR series tracks the mixed G2/TEP Mg(OTf)2 electrolyte from 313.2 K down to 243.2 K. The dominant, robust finding is a slow-to-fast chemical-exchange transition governing TEP speciation. At low temperature (243.2, 258.2 K) three resolved 31P environments are present, with a very broad dominant component (FWHM up to 3.38 ppm) — the hallmark of intermediate/slow exchange between distinct TEP solvation states (free TEP near -5.5/-6 ppm and Mg-coordinated TEP near -3.5 ppm), plus an additional inner-shoulder environment resolved only by the 3-Voigt fit. Between 258.2 and 278.2 K the resolved-species count collapses to 1, and above this the single peak sharpens progressively (0.98→0.36→0.19 ppm) toward a motionally averaged fast-exchange resonance. The apparent 'dominant' chemical shift is non-monotonic (and its linear/Arrhenius regressions are near-meaningless, R²~0.15-0.19) precisely because the 'dominant' label maps to different physical entities across the coalescence — a coalesced population-weighted average at high T versus a resolved single environment at low T — so scatter there is expected rather than a fit failure. Fit quality improves monotonically with T as lineshapes simplify. The residual structure is physically informative and clusters in the transition region: at low T the residuals reflected genuine under-resolution (fixed by adding a component), while at mid T (278.2, 293.5 K) coherent single-sign-change dispersive S-shaped residuals straddle the apex. This asymmetry is consistent with incomplete coalescence (a not-quite-averaged shoulder) but is also the textbook signature of a small phase error; the F-test rejected an extra component and phase correction was outside the locked constraints, so these two explanations remain degenerate on the present data. The locked model's design (T-dependent Voigt count) matches the exchange interpretation and thereby captures the dominant physics well; relaxation narrowing (with T1 data available) may contribute to FWHM trends but cannot account for the species-count change and is therefore secondary. A key reporting limitation: no Larmor frequency was in the metadata, so FWHM is available only in ppm (not Hz) and no T2* estimate can be quoted, weakening quantitative separation of exchange vs relaxation contributions to linewidth.

scientific_claims.claim: The 31P NMR of the G2/TEP Mg(OTf)2 electrolyte undergoes a slow-to-fast chemical-exchange transition with increasing temperature: three resolved TEP-solvation environments at low T (243-258 K) coalesce into a single motionally-averaged, progressively narrowing resonance above ~278 K, evidencing temperature-controlled competitive solvation exchange between free and Mg-coordinated TEP.
scientific_claims.scientific_impact: Directly characterizes how temperature governs the speciation and solvation dynamics of the active cation in a mixed-solvent Mg electrolyte, which controls ion transport and coordination-shell composition relevant to battery performance.
scientific_claims.has_anyone_question: Has anyone quantified the temperature-dependent exchange kinetics (coalescence temperature and exchange rate) between free and Mg-coordinated TEP in mixed diglyme/triethyl-phosphate Mg electrolytes using variable-temperature 31P NMR?

issues.problem: Systematic dispersive (S-shaped) residual straddling the peak center — the single Voigt does not reproduce the true lineshape. The zoomed region -7.8 to -2.3 shows a coherent positive lobe on the left flank/top and a negative lobe just past the center (1 sign-change), the classic signature of a lineshape mismatch (asymmetry or an unresolved second component), not random noise.
Reported component count is inconsistent (header says 2 components; FITTED PARAMETERS lists only peak_1 with component_count = 1). Only a single Voigt is actually parameterized/plotted.

verification_iterations.fix_applied: Refine the Voigt center/FWHM/L-G mixing (and check baseline/phase) to remove the S-shaped residual near x≈-4 to -2; reconcile the component-count discrepancy before quoting integrated intensity.

verification_iterations.model: Voigt profile(s) on a linear baseline for the resonance near -3.5 ppm. Primary component: 1 broad Voigt whose center, FWHM, and Gaussian/Lorentzian mixing fraction (eta) are all free parameters, allowing the L/G balance to capture the true flank curvature rather than defaulting to a fixed shape. A second Voigt (unresolved shoulder / incomplete-coalescence component) is retained as an optional component, added only if an F-test on the residual justifies it. The linear baseline (slope + offset) is fit jointly but constrained to the peak-free wings so it does not absorb genuine peak curvature. The persistent S-shaped (dispersive) residual straddling the center is treated within the locked Voigt model as a lineshape mismatch to be absorbed by (a) refined center/FWHM/L-G mixing and, if F-test-justified, (b) a second Voigt representing the slow-exchange partner; residual phase error is flagged but only correctable if the constraint level later permits.

flagged_spectra_analysis.summary: No spectra were formally flagged (all R^2 >= 0.996, all approved). However, verification histories reveal systematic, physically meaningful residual structure concentrated at low-to-mid temperature: under-resolution at 243-258 K (resolved by adding components) and coherent dispersive S-shaped apex residuals at 278.2 and 293.5 K.
possible_causes: Incomplete coalescence producing a slightly asymmetric near-averaged lineshape that a symmetric Voigt cannot fully reproduce
Small residual phase error at mid-T (dispersive S-shaped residual is a classic phase-error signature); flagged by fitter but not correctable under locked constraints
Genuine unresolved second component rejected by F-test (small residual, does not meet acceptance)
recommended_followup: Re-phase the mid-T (278.2, 293.5 K) spectra and refit to test whether the S-shaped residual is phase-related or genuine lineshape asymmetry
Acquire/record the Larmor frequency to report FWHM in Hz and estimate T2*, separating exchange from relaxation contributions
Use the accompanying T1 (and if available T2) relaxation data plus lineshape simulation across the full 30-spectrum VT set to extract the exchange rate and coalescence temperature
flagged_spectra_analysis.scientific_significance: The clustering of systematic residuals within the coalescence window corroborates the exchange interpretation and pinpoints the temperature range where exchange is intermediate — the most kinetically informative region for extracting exchange rates.

refit_analysis.summary: No adaptive refit to a different model class occurred. Within the locked Voigt-on-linear-baseline class, the low-T spectra were fit with 3 Voigts rather than the nominal 2, and mid-T spectra used a single pseudo-Voigt with a free L/G mixing fraction.
model_changes: 243.2 K and 258.2 K: 2->3 Voigt components added to resolve a real inner-shoulder environment between the horns (data-driven, same model class)
278.2 K and 293.5 K: single pseudo-Voigt with free L/G mixing (eta) to attempt capturing flank curvature; second component F-test-rejected
refit_analysis.scientific_implications: The component-count increases are data-driven and consistent with more than two resolved TEP environments at the lowest temperatures, reinforcing the competitive-solvation exchange picture rather than indicating a fit artifact. The count is data-driven (verified via F-test and residual inspection), so the 3->1 discontinuity should be read as a real structural/exchange transition, not a locked-count artifact.

Interpretation: transition from multi-component (slow-exchange, resolved TEP solvation environments) at low T toward a single motionally-averaged peak at high T indicates fast competitive solvation exchange between G2 and TEP as temperature increases.

resolved_species_count.interpretation: Stepwise drop from 3 environments at low T (243-258 K) to 1 at high T (278-313 K); marks the slow-to-fast exchange (coalescence) transition between free and Mg-coordinated TEP solvation states.

dominant_FWHM_ppm.interpretation: Strong narrowing with temperature (3.38 ppm at 243 K to 0.19 ppm at 313 K), consistent with reduced exchange broadening as the system moves into the fast-exchange regime; possible secondary T2* relaxation contribution (not separable without Larmor frequency for Hz conversion).

dominant_chemical_shift_ppm.interpretation: Poorly described by linear or Arrhenius regression (R^2~0.15-0.19) because the 'dominant' peak represents different physical species (resolved environment vs coalesced average) across the transition; not interpretable as a single continuous shift.

fit_r_squared.interpretation: Monotonic improvement with temperature as lineshapes simplify from broad/multi-component (low T) to sharp single peaks (high T); reflects fit tractability, not solely data quality.

caveats: The 'dominant chemical shift' maps to different physical species across the coalescence, so its non-monotonic behavior and near-zero regression R^2 are expected and should NOT be interpreted as a continuous shift trend or an Arrhenius relation. No Larmor frequency was in the metadata: FWHM is reported in ppm only, precluding Hz conversion and T2* estimation, so exchange vs relaxation contributions to linewidth cannot be quantitatively separated from these five spectra alone. The mid-T dispersive S-shaped apex residual is left unresolved by the symmetric-Voigt model and is ambiguous between genuine near-coalescence asymmetry and a small phase error (phase correction was outside the locked constraint level) — this is a model-vs-evidence divergence that does not overturn the exchange interpretation but warrants re-phasing/refit. Only 5 of the stated 30 VT spectra are summarized here; coalescence temperature and exchange rates should be extracted from the full ladder plus the T1 relaxation data rather than asserted from this subset. Species assignments (free TEP vs Mg-coordinated TEP) are inherited from the model design and are chemically reasonable given the 31P shift range but are not independently verified here.

locked_fitting_config.analysis_approach: Fit each spectrum with a sum of Voigt profiles on a linear baseline over the full ±41→+47 ppm range. Let the component count be data-driven per temperature: 1 Voigt in the fast-exchange (high-T) regime, 2 Voigts in the slow-exchange (low-T) regime, with intermediate temperatures decided by whether a second component materially improves the peak-region fit. Track δ_iso, FWHM, and integral vs temperature and report the component count vs temperature — the coalescence temperature is the key deliverable for the competitive-solvation objective.
locked_fitting_config.physical_model: Sum of Voigt profiles (Lorentzian-dominant, Gaussian width free for shim/disorder) on a linear baseline: 1 Voigt for fast-exchange spectra (~-2.5 to -3.5 ppm), 2 Voigts for slow-exchange spectra (free TEP + Mg-coordinated TEP, ~-5.5 and ~-3.5 ppm).
locked_fitting_config.fitting_strategy: Lock lineshape form (Voigt) and baseline form (linear) across the whole series so shifts/widths stay comparable; do NOT lock component count. Fit signal region peaks; report peak_region_r2 not global R². Initial guesses: single peak at ~-2.5 ppm (313 K), ~-3.5 ppm (278 K); two peaks at ~-5.5 and ~-3.5 ppm (243 K). Amplitudes positive (phase is correct). Use least-squares (Levenberg-Marquardt / trust-region). For borderline intermediate temperatures, apply an F-test to justify adding the second Voigt. Mask any single-point DC glitch exactly at 0 ppm if present. No sidebands (solution-state, no MAS).
